figures.caption: Fig. 1. The proposed Multi-Layer Navigation System (MLNS) for a smart wheelchair semi-autonomous navigation. Given the user and OpenNav inputs, a PQ combined with MPC and ViSPF controls the navigation of the wheelchair.

Fig. 4. A) Normalized heatmaps of the aggregated trajectories produced during the experiments (center). B-D) Normalized heatmaps of the trajectories divided per target and modality. White dashed lines represent the average Baseline path for each target. Heatmap represents a color gradient of the crossed positions, from the more (in yellow) to the less (in blue) common.

Fig. 5. Distribution of the paths length traveled for each target and navigation modality. Horizontal brackets indicate pairs with a statistically significant difference (Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn’s post-hoc test, p < 0.05)
Fig. 6. Distribution of the completion time (top) and number of commands sent by the user (bottom) of each target.
